strengths: Clear and unified conceptual formulation: The introduction of 'input controllability' and 'output controllability' provides an elegant, modular abstraction that cleanly decouples internal activation preservation from residual difference absorption across various modern architectural components (gated MLPs, bias-free formulations, RMSNorm, MoE, and parallel blocks).

Rigorous extension beyond vanilla transformers: Prior works (e.g., Dherin et al., 2025; Innocenti & Achour, 2025) relied heavily on additive output biases or vanilla MLP structures. This paper successfully bridges the gap to state-of-the-art LLM architectures (such as Gemma and Falcon) that omit biases and employ non-linear gating and RMS normalization.

Careful treatment of numerical stability: The authors not only prove mathematical equivalence in exact arithmetic but also recognize the practical failure modes of low-precision (bfloat16) representations due to element-wise divisions near zero. The analytical RMSNorm inversion derived via Lagrange multipliers (Appendix B) is well-motivated, mathematically sound, and effectively restores 100% token fidelity.

Thorough theoretical and empirical validation: The theoretical claims (including impossibility results in Theorem 4) are supported by detailed proofs and solid empirical verification on modern models (Gemma 3 and Falcon 7B) across both text and multimodal contexts.
weaknesses: Descriptive rather than practical inference technique: Because the rank-1 updates are token-dependent and require forward-pass intermediate activations to compute, the procedure cannot currently serve as an efficient inference mechanism without aggregation techniques (e.g., as explored in concurrent work by Mazzawi et al., 2025).

Limited generation length and benchmark diversity: Experimental validation is primarily demonstrated on relatively short generations (10–25 tokens) across a small set of prompts. Evaluating cumulative error drift over longer autoregressive contexts (e.g., hundreds of tokens) or standardized ICL benchmarks would provide stronger empirical grounding.

Gap between mathematical equivalence and internal computation: While the paper proves that context can be analytically compiled into rank-1 parameter patches, this existence proof does not establish that the transformer's internal representations or attention heads are actively performing these specific weight-update dynamics during standard inference.

strengths: Meaningful theoretical generalization: The paper successfully extends prior theoretical results (e.g., Dherin et al., 2025; Innocenti & Achour, 2025) from simplified vanilla transformers with biases to realistic modern LLM architectures, including bias-free layers, gated MLPs (SwiGLU/GeGLU), pre/post-RMSNorm, MoE, and parallel blocks.

Unifying and elegant conceptual framework: The definitions of input controllability and output controllability provide an intuitive, modular lens to evaluate whether an arbitrary residual block architecture can absorb context into parameter patches.

Rigorous treatment of numerical stability and edge cases: Rather than ignoring practical failure modes, the authors explicitly diagnose issues like division-by-zero/near-zero in post-RMSNorm updates, derive a constrained analytical RMSNorm inversion via Lagrange multipliers (Appendix B), and formally establish impossibility bounds for post-RMSNorm lacking trainable scales (Theorem 4).

Thorough empirical verification: The authors validate their theoretical claims on modern open models (Gemma 3 1B/4B and Falcon-7B) across both text and multimodal (image) contexts, demonstrating exact token-level matching and near-zero logit differences under float32 and stabilized bfloat16.
weaknesses: Fundamental mathematical simplicity: At its core, the equivalence relies on the standard minimal Frobenius-norm solution to the underdetermined linear equation $\Delta W z = y$ (i.e., $\Delta W = y z^\top / \|z\|^2$) paired with residual compensation. While the architectural adaptations and RMSNorm inversion are neat, the core algebraic mechanism is relatively elementary.

Limited practical standalone utility: Because the parameter patches are strictly token-dependent and must be recomputed at every autoregressive step, the method cannot yet be deployed as an efficient inference mechanism or global prompt compressor without additional aggregation heuristics.

Small empirical sample size: Although the theoretical proofs are exact, the empirical demonstrations in Section 4 and Appendix C are demonstrated on a limited set of hand-picked prompts rather than evaluated systematically across standard in-context learning benchmark datasets.

Heuristic connection to meta-learning: The connection to gradient descent in Appendix E relies on defining an artificial trace pseudo-loss constructed specifically so that its gradient recovers the additive patch, which is somewhat tautological and does not substantiate whether the model's forward pass organically optimizes a semantic objective.

strengths: Generalizes the implicit weight-patch theory of in-context learning (Dherin et al., 2025; Innocenti & Achour, 2025) to modern architectural components: bias-free layers, gated MLPs (SwiGLU/GeGLU), pre- and post-RMSNorm, and Mixture-of-Experts.

Introduces an elegant and unifying conceptual framework based on 'input controllability' and 'output controllability' (Theorem 3), which clarifies the conditions under which attention effects can be absorbed into MLP sub-layers.

Identifies practical numerical failure modes arising from element-wise division by near-zero activations in lower precision (bfloat16) and develops a mathematically principled workaround using constrained RMSNorm inversion via Lagrange multipliers (Appendix B).

Provides an impossibility proof (Theorem 4) showing that exact equivalence fails geometrically for post-RMSNorm blocks without a trainable scaling vector, delineating the theoretical boundaries of the framework.

Empirically verifies the mathematical equivalences on modern open-weight LLMs (Gemma 3 1B/4B, Falcon 7B) across text and multimodal contexts, measuring logit discrepancies, total variation distance, and token matching.
weaknesses: The underlying algebraic construction relies on an elementary rank-1 projection trick to map vector z to z_C (i.e., Delta W = W(z_C - z)z^T / ||z||^2); while its application across composite modern blocks is neat, the core mathematical novelty over Dherin et al. (2025) is relatively incremental.

As acknowledged by the authors, the parameter updates are strictly token- and step-dependent, requiring full activation caching and recomputation at every autoregressive step. Consequently, the work serves primarily as an analytical/interpretability lens rather than an actionable inference-time optimization or compression technique.

The empirical evaluation functions essentially as a numerical sanity check of the derived identities on a handful of short generation prompts, rather than evaluating downstream utility on broader standard benchmarks or mechanistic interpretability tasks (e.g., locating or steering specific ICL capabilities).
